name: The core's activities
about: What can be done with any historical object, whatever its kind: it is presented, inquired into by the four questions, traced through what it rested on, and examined in what is said of it and what the archive holds of it.

activities.name: Inquire
activities.about: The four questions asked of every object: what problem it answers, why that problem arose, what made it answerable, and to whom it mattered and what it made possible.

activities.name: Present
activities.about: What the object is, when and where, and what it stands under.

activities.name: Trace
activities.about: What its appearing rested on, step by step, and what rests on it.

activities.name: Examine
activities.about: What is said of it, by whom and how it stands; the materials the archive holds of it.

tours.name: The circle that would not close

stops.say: One string and a movable bridge: on it a ratio of two lengths can be seen and heard at once. Much of what follows rests on this.
A scale built from pure fifths alone. Ask what made it possible, and what it left unsolved.
Far to the east, on pitch pipes and not on a string, the same scale is reached by a rule of thirds. The record knows no tie between the two.
Both meet the same trouble: twelve fifths overshoot seven octaves, and the scale never returns to where it began. The problem arises twice, each time of its own cause.
One answer: go on. Sixty pitches, and the fifty-fourth lies very near the first.
In Europe another problem presses first: thirds that are harsh in harmony. Narrow every fifth a little and the thirds turn pure. Play the fifths, and hear the one that pays for it.
In 1584 the circle is closed exactly, by the twelfth root of two. See what had to be there first.

Within a year or so, on the other side of the world, the same answer, by a man who has argued that a root is a number like any other. Ask who else answered this problem, and whether they knew of each other.
And in 1722 a book of music in every key, for a keyboard that is well tempered. What it rested on took two thousand years.
